submitter_note: MLA Scott Cyr, Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul (with joint northern MLAs' proposal and City of Cold Lake letter attached)
community: Saddle Lake Cree Nation; Buffalo Lake and Kikino Métis Settlements; Whitefish Lake (White Fish Lake Reserve)
request: Move Saddle Lake Cree Nation from Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul to Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock (Cyr, May 2025); the attached joint northern MLAs' proposal also moves Buffalo Lake, Kikino and White Fish Lake Reserve from Fort McMurray-Lac La Biche to Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock and keeps some portion of Saddle Lake there.
quote: Transfer Saddle Lake Cree Nation from Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul and place it within Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock
note: Several documents in one record. Cyr's May letter (pp.29-37) asks Saddle Lake be moved to ABW, rationale population. Joint northern MLAs' proposal (pp.38-46, p.42-43): 'Transfer Buffalo Lake and Kikino Métis settlements, and White Fish Lake Reserve to Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock' and 'sections of St Paul County should remain in Athabasca - Barrhead - Westlock as should some portion of the Saddle Lake Reserve'; keeps Heart Lake and Beaver Lake reserves in Fort McMurray-Lac La Biche. Cyr's Dec letter (pp.56-60) supports the interim Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul boundary and asks to keep CLAWR in the riding, citing Cold Lake FN / Frog Lake ties to the range (not a request about reserve placement). Submitters are MLAs, not nation bodies.
Indigenous only in proposed riding name honouring Alexander Decoteau.
'Stoney' is Stoney Trail.

submitter_note: Mayor Andrew Knack, City of Edmonton
request: Do not create the hybrid Edmonton-West-Enoch riding combining west Edmonton with Enoch Cree Nation and Parkland County; keep Edmonton ridings within city boundaries.
quote: The proposal to create a hybrid electoral division (Edmonton-West-Enoch), blending urban West Edmonton, Enoch Cree Nation, and Parkland County, risks a fundamental misalignment of representative concerns
note: Objection is mainly to the urban-rural hybrid for Edmonton's sake; implies Enoch not be with west Edmonton but names no district for Enoch.
Siksika only in the district name Cardston-Siksika.

submitter_note: Indigenous rights lawyer, resident of Ritchie, Edmonton-Strathcona
community: Mackenzie riding First Nations; Fort Chipewyan, Conklin, Anzac, Janvier
request: Keep the new Indigenous-focused Mackenzie riding; and suggests a predominantly rural riding joining Lac La Biche with Fort Chipewyan, Conklin, Anzac and Janvier as a second riding with a large Indigenous population.
quote: It should also be noted that having a predominantly rural riding in and near Fort McMurray would facilitate a second riding with a large Indigenous population
note: Supports Mackenzie ('I commend the EBC's recommendation to create the riding of Mackenzie', p.93). The Lac La Biche suggestion names communities (Janvier = Chipewyan Prairie area), not reserves by name. Rest of letter is about Edmonton seats.
'Stoney' is Stoney Trail.

community: First Nations near High Level; Peerless Trout
request: Do not group the First Nations near High Level with distant First Nations such as Peerless Trout in a predominantly Indigenous Mackenzie riding; keep them with High Level and neighbouring northwest municipalities.
quote: grouping these communities with other First Nations such as Peerless Trout, which is geographically distant and has distinct economic and cultural circumstances, does not reflect these realities
note: Opposes Mackenzie as 'unintended segregation'. Quote begins on p.115.

submitter_note: MLA Jason Nixon, Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre
community: O'Chiese First Nation 203, Sunchild First Nation 202, Big Horn 144A, Stoney 142, 143, 144
request: Create a west central riding with Clearwater County, Rocky Mountain House, Sundre, MD of Bighorn and Banff that includes O'Chiese 203, Sunchild 202, Big Horn 144A and Stoney 142, 143 and 144.
quote: O’Chiese First Nation 203, Sunchild First Nation 202, and Big Horn 144A
note: Reserves listed in his conclusion as components of the proposed riding; the rationale is Eastern Slopes communities of interest, not the nations' wishes. Stoney 142-144 are Morley-area Stoney reserves.

submitter_note: President, Indigenous Bar Association in Canada
community: 13 First Nations and 4 Métis settlements in proposed Mackenzie riding
request: Keep the proposed Mackenzie riding that brings together northern Indigenous voters (13 First Nations, 4 Métis settlements).
quote: We urge the Commission to preserve the Mackenzie riding as presented in the interim proposal
note: IBA is a national association of Indigenous lawyers, not a nation or council government; coded non_member for that reason.

request: Keep the Banff-Jasper division that puts all six Stoney reserves and the Tsuut'ina reserve under a single MLA.
quote: representation of this population block by a single MLA will strengthen the Indigenous views brought to the Legislature
note: Describes interim map as encompassing all 6 Stoney reserves and Tsuut'ina, previously in three divisions.

request: Move the Banff-Jasper eastern boundary west so more of Clearwater County, including Sunchild and O'Chiese, is in Lacombe-Rocky Mountain House.

note: Placement of Sunchild/O'Chiese in Lacombe-Rocky Mountain House is implied by the boundary move to trunk road 734, not stated outright.

submitter_note: Mayor Francesca Ward, on behalf of Town of Slave Lake Council
community: Treaty 8 First Nations and Métis communities of the Lesser Slave Lake region (Sawridge, Bigstone Cree, Driftpile, Sucker Creek, Peerless/Trout, Peavine, Gift Lake, East Prairie)
request: Retain the Lesser Slave Lake riding and keep its Treaty 8 First Nations and Métis communities together (including Sawridge First Nation with Slave Lake, MD of Lesser Slave River, Big Lakes and MD of Opportunity), rather than splitting Bigstone/Peerless-Trout from Sawridge/Driftpile/Sucker Creek.
quote: Maintain electoral divisions that concentrate Treaty 8 First Nations and Métis communities, rather than dispersing them
note: Town council report, not a nation body. P.114-115 objects that First Nations 'will be split among at least two ridings (Bigstone, Peerless/Trout in one; Sawridge, Driftpile, Sucker Creek in another)'. Recommendation 4 (p.116) keeps Sawridge FN with Slave Lake, MD Lesser Slave River, Big Lakes, MD Opportunity. Also suggests adding Calling Lake area.
Indigenous communities listed only as a general factor.
